title: HSM session-proxy Terraform provider shim for secrets routing and upgrade safety
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a Terraform provider-style module (shim) and operator-friendly Terraform resources that manage an HSM session-proxy for Private (VPC) deployments. The shim will standardize how Redwood Private initializes, rotates, and monitors HSM-backed key sessions across Vault and AWS Secrets Manager backends, and provide safe upgrade/rollback semantics for upgrades to HSM firmware, PKCS#11 libraries, and provider modules.
background: Customers deploying Redwood Private often run HSMs (cloud HSM, on-prem HSM appliance) behind VPCs. Current Terraform recipes are ad-hoc: direct PKCS#11 calls in bootstrap scripts, brittle rotation windows, and no centralized health checks. Upgrades to HSM firmware or the PKCS#11 stack have caused production incidents in the past. We need a repeatable IaC abstraction that operators can use during initial provisioning and during rolling upgrades.
proposal: Build a Terraform module and companion lightweight session-proxy container that exposes a stable TLS gRPC API for key operations. The Terraform resources will:
proposal_details: Provision session-proxy deployment (k8s Deployment or ECS Service) with CR/Lifecycle hooks
Create 'redwood_hsm_session' resource that binds an HSM logical partition (slot) to a named key client, issuing ephemeral session tokens stored in Secrets Manager or Vault depending on config
Support dual-write mode: simultaneously write key metadata into Vault and AWS Secrets Manager for migrations
Expose healthchecks: liveness (response to PKCS#11 info), readiness (session allocation within threshold), and a hardware-error probe (nonzero HSM alarm codes)
Provide lifecycle policies and runbooks for canary firmware upgrades, rolling driver restarts, and graceful session draining
Offer diagnostic metrics (session_count, session_alloc_latency_ms, pkcs11_errors_total) via Prometheus endpoint mounted by the session-proxy
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published to internal registry with versioned releases and examples for Vault-only, SecretsManager-only, and dual-write migrations
E2E test runs against a lab HSM (cloud HSM emulator) demonstrate successful key provisioning, rotation, and forced failover
Healthchecks surface meaningful signals in Console (alerts on session_alloc_latency_ms > 200ms or pkcs11_errors_total > 1/min)
Canary upgrade playbook verified: upgrade 10% of nodes, monitor metrics for 10 minutes, proceed or rollback
Security review completed and KMS/HSM audit logs integrated into customer audit trail
tasks: Design: finalize gRPC API and secrets schema (Ava)
Container: build lightweight session-proxy binary with pkcs11 and metrics (SRE)
Operator hooks: k8s readiness/lifecycle and ECS drain integration (Infra)
Testing: lab HSM harness, chaos tests for HSM disconnects (QA)
Docs: runbook + upgrade playbook + Confluence design doc (PM/Docs)
Security: threat model and SOC/pen-test coordination (Security)
risks: HSM vendor differences: PKCS#11 behavior varies across appliances (Mitigation: vendor adapters and integration tests)
Secrets dual-write inconsistency during migrations (Mitigation: idempotent writers and verification step)
Upgrade-induced session storms causing latency blips (Mitigation: staggered canary and drain windows)
Operator-facing complexity: exposing too many knobs in Terraform (Mitigation: sane defaults + opinionated presets)
Regulatory: storing ephemeral session tokens in cloud secrets may be unacceptable to some customers (Mitigation: support HSM-backed key IDs without token persistence)
Performance: proxy adds minimal latency but must be measured and bounded (Mitigation: local caching and connection pooling)
testing_plan: Unit tests for Terraform resource lifecycle with terratest
Integration tests against SoftHSM and AWS CloudHSM in a CI lab
Chaos test: simulate HSM disconnect and verify graceful failover to fallback model variant
Perf: load test session allocation to measure  p95 allocation latency < 200ms
Upgrade test: run full canary and rollback in lab with automated verification script
rollout_plan: Publish v0.1.0 to internal registry and mark as experimental
Deploy session-proxy to staging clusters and run acceptance tests
Enable module for 2 pilot customers with Dedicated capacity (opt-in), monitor 72 hours
Iterate on feedback, then schedule broader rollout with 10%/30%/60% canary windows
Add to 'private-2026.04' release notes and training materials
rollback_plan: Terraform: apply previous module version pin and restore previous session-proxy container image
Run verification to confirm session tokens are served by rollback proxy
If hardware-level failure, follow HSM vendor emergency procedure and escalate
Postmortem capturing timeline and metric deltas
